differences.title: 1. Data Compression
differences.leftDesc: TimescaleDB leverages PostgreSQL's columnar compression, offering efficient storage and query performance by organizing data in columns for analytical workloads.
differences.rightDesc: InfluxDB employs time-based compression, optimizing for high-frequency writes and reads by compressing adjacent data points with similar timestamps.

differences.title: 2. Ingestion Throughput
differences.leftDesc: TimescaleDB's ingestion performance is tied to PostgreSQL's tuning capabilities, benefiting from mature connection pooling and WAL mechanisms.
differences.rightDesc: InfluxDB is engineered for extremely high ingestion rates, featuring a dedicated write path and optimized buffering for continuous data streams.

differences.title: 3. Retention Policies
differences.leftDesc: TimescaleDB manages data retention using standard SQL `DELETE` statements, often automated with `cron` jobs or scheduled tasks.
differences.rightDesc: InfluxDB offers native, declarative retention policies that automatically expire or downsample data based on defined time durations.

differences.title: 4. SQL Support
differences.leftDesc: TimescaleDB provides full PostgreSQL SQL compliance, allowing seamless integration with existing SQL tools and expertise for querying.
differences.rightDesc: InfluxDB uses Flux, a powerful functional data scripting language, offering advanced time-series analysis and transformation capabilities.

differences.title: 5. Ecosystem Integration
differences.leftDesc: Leverages PostgreSQL's extensive driver support, ORMs, and tooling, making integration straightforward for many applications.
differences.rightDesc: Integrates well with its own TICK stack (Telegraf, InfluxDB, Chronograf, Kapacitor) and other monitoring tools.

differences.title: 6. Data Model Flexibility
differences.leftDesc: TimescaleDB uses traditional relational tables, providing familiar structure and the ability to join with other relational data.
differences.rightDesc: InfluxDB uses a schema of measurements, tags (indexed metadata), and fields (time-series values).

differences.title: 7. Distributed Architecture
differences.leftDesc: TimescaleDB scales using PostgreSQL's proven clustering technologies like Citus, offering horizontal scalability for large deployments.
differences.rightDesc: InfluxDB Enterprise offers distributed capabilities out-of-the-box, designed for multi-node deployments and high availability.
